newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-60,000 Mercedes workers walk out-union.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-60,000 Mercedes workers walk out-union.

text.p: A total of 60,000 Mercedes-Benz workers staged temporary walkouts throughout Germany on Thursday in protest at possible cuts in sick pay, union officials said.
The protests caused losses to the Daimler-Benz car-making unit of around 800 passsenger cars and 100 trucks, a spokeswoman for the Baden-Wuerttemberg branch of the IG Metall engineering union said.

The biggest action took place at Mercedes' largest passenger car plant in Sindelfingen near Stuttgart. About 15,000 workers temporarily downed tools on the early and day shifts to gather for a demonstration outside the factory gates and left before the end of their shifts.

The protest follows the breakdown on Wednesday of talks between the IG Metall trade union and the Gesamtmetall employers federation over proposed cuts to labour costs such as sick pay and the wider 1997 pay round.

A similar protest took place earlier this month at the Untertuerkheim plant, also near Stuttgart, after Daimler-Benz AG said it would implement a new law cutting sick pay to 80 percent of salary from the current 100 percent.
About the same number of employees as in Thursday's protest were involved. Mercedes estimated then it cost some 80 million marks ($52.52 million) in lost production.
Daimler and other large engineering employers have since backed down on the cuts, saying they will wait until new work contracts can be agreed with unions.
But the companies have made it clear they see sick pay cuts or comparable measures as necessary to boost their international competitivity.
